editorial:
If you want a silly family comedy where animals talk and help a zookeeper find love, this one delivers goofy charm. Griffin Keyes is great with animals but awkward around people, especially after his proposal to Stephanie flopped years ago. When she comes back, the zoo animals secretly talk and coach him on romance, leading to funny lessons, awkward dates, and plenty of animal chaos. It’s light, silly, and easy to watch with kids. The zoo setting gives it a warm, friendly backdrop, and the animal characters steal many scenes.

Kevin James brings his usual everyman energy, and the animal voices add silly fun, though some jokes feel predictable. The romance is simple, and the pacing stays brisk enough for a family night. If you enjoy talking-animal comedies and don’t mind goofy humor, it’s a decent pick. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for a movie night.
endingExplained: Griffin realizes Stephanie only likes the fake alpha-male version of him, while his coworker Kate truly cares about him. The animals help him see that being himself matters more than impressing Stephanie. In the end, Griffin chooses Kate, and the zoo animals celebrate as he finally finds real love and happiness. He also keeps his zoo job and stays close to the animals who helped him.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves family comedies, talking animals, and goofy romance.
